issue: The figure title calls the routing a 'sequential cascade', but the caption calls it a 'decision tree' and the prose says 'only ONE model is selected per request (early exit on a match)'. In AI systems, 'cascade' conventionally implies multiple models invoked in sequence, which contradicts the early-exit routing shown.
evidence: Title: 'Routing every request to the right specialised model (sequential cascade)'. Caption: 'Model-routing decision tree'. Prose: 'only ONE model is selected per request (early exit on a match)'.
acceptance_test: Retitle to 'sequential routing decision tree (early exit)' or define 'routing cascade' explicitly; use the same term in title, caption, and prose.

figure: FIGURE 18.1 (Routing every request to the right specialised model)
issue: The in-figure title uses British spelling 'specialised' while the caption and the surrounding text use American 'specialist'/'specialized'.
evidence: Figure title: 'Routing every request to the right specialised model (sequential cascade)'. Caption: '...with the specialist, general-purpose and fallback model families as leaves' and 'Each specialized family is a leaf of the router'. The rest of the book uses American spelling ('summarize', 'quantization').
acceptance_test: Change the figure title to 'Routing every request to the right specialized model (sequential cascade)' and confirm the spelling matches the caption and the book's house style.

issue: The 'yes → specialist' branch fans out from the Capability filter to three specialist boxes (Embedding, Vision, Math/reason) without a selector node or a label saying 'one of'. The prose says only one model is selected per request, so the fan-out can be misread as invoking all three specialists.
evidence: Single 'yes → specialist' arrow from Capability filter to a horizontal connector feeding Embedding, Vision, and Math/reason; prose: 'only ONE model is selected per request (early exit on a match)'.
acceptance_test: Add a selector node or label the fan-out 'specialist family (one selected)' so the diagram cannot imply all three are invoked.

issue: The note is a run-on: the parenthetical '(early exit on a match)' is followed immediately by 'policy:' with no separator, so the sentence reads as if 'policy' were inside the parenthesis.
evidence: Printed note: 'only ONE model is selected per request (early exit on a match) policy: capability first, then cost/SLO, then general fallback.'
acceptance_test: Rewrite as 'only ONE model is selected per request (early exit on a match) — policy: capability first, then cost/SLO, then general fallback.' and confirm the note is set at >= 8 pt.

figure: FIGURE 18.1, edge labels and leaf colours
issue: The 'no' edge labels are the smallest type in the figure and are set in a colour that is not explained, while the three specialist leaves use two different fills (blue for Embedding/Vision, dark red for Math/reason) with no stated meaning — inviting the reader to infer a distinction that does not exist.
evidence: The two 'no' labels sit above the top-row arrows in small grey type; the 'yes -> specialist' and 'yes -> frontier / small' labels are green. The leaf row shows Embedding and Vision in blue and Math/reason in dark red, with no legend explaining the difference.
acceptance_test: Set the 'no' labels at the same size as the 'yes' labels and add a one-line legend ('green = match, grey = no match') or drop the colour coding in favour of uniform label styling; give the three specialist leaves a single fill. Confirm all labels are >= 8 pt in the print proof and that the yes/no distinction survives grayscale.

issue: The in-figure title uses the British spelling 'specialised' ('Routing every request to the right specialised model (sequential cascade)'), which may conflict with the US '-ize' house style used in body text. The caption on the same page uses the noun 'specialist', so the only -ise/-ize occurrence on the page is the in-figure adjective.
evidence: In-figure bold title: 'Routing every request to the right specialised model (sequential cascade)'.
acceptance_test: Grep the source for 'specializ'/'specialis'; the in-figure title's spelling must match the dominant body-text convention for the same word (expected 'specialized' for a US-Letter book). If the book is uniformly -ise, no change.

issue: The title/caption call the diagram a 'four-state machine', but the drawing contains six state-like boxes: Plan, Execute, Observe, Decide, Final answer, and Stopped. The two terminal boxes are visually identical to the loop states, so a reader can reasonably count six states.
evidence: Title: 'The agent loop: a four-state machine'. Caption: 'four-state machine (Plan, Execute, Observe, Decide)'. Diagram boxes: Plan, Execute, Observe, Decide, Final answer, Stopped.
acceptance_test: Retitle to 'four-state agent loop with two terminal outcomes' or redraw Final answer/Stopped as terminal outcomes rather than state boxes.

figure: FIGURE 19.1 (The agent loop: a four-state machine)
issue: The figure is rendered at roughly 55–60% of the text-block width, which forces its role annotations and edge labels to be the smallest type in the book; the state machine is the chapter's central mental model and is currently under-sized for the page it occupies.
evidence: The four state boxes plus the two terminal boxes occupy about half the measure, leaving large empty margins left and right. The italic role words ('model', 'action', 'state', 'check'), the sub-labels ('read, plan', 'tool call', 'append result', 'resolved?') and the edge labels ('loop (iterate) — not resolved', 'resolved', 'limit hit') are all visibly smaller than the caption's type.
acceptance_test: Enlarge the figure to the full text measure (or split the state machine and the terminal-state outcomes into two stacked panels at full width) and measure the smallest annotation in the print proof: it must be >= 8 pt. Confirm the enlarged figure does not push the caption to the next page.

issue: The 'resolved' label is positioned in the junction where the dashed loop-back line, the Decide-to-Final-answer arrow and the Decide-to-Stopped arrow meet, so it is ambiguous which edge it annotates.
evidence: The word 'resolved' sits immediately below the dashed 'loop (iterate) — not resolved' line and above the 'Final answer' box, on the vertical segment that also carries the 'limit hit' branch. A reader can plausibly read 'resolved' as labelling the dashed loop-back edge (whose own label already says 'not resolved'), which would invert the meaning.
acceptance_test: Move 'resolved' onto the Decide -> Final answer edge (offset to the left of that segment, clear of the dashed line) and 'limit hit' onto the Decide -> Stopped edge, with each label >= 3 pt from any other line or label. Verify at 300 dpi that no label can be read as belonging to a different edge.

issue: Six different fill colours are used with no legend and no stated semantics, so colour appears to encode something that it does not.
evidence: Plan is blue, Execute and Observe are green, Decide is pink, Final answer is purple, Stopped is orange; the italic role words are coloured to match. Nothing in the figure or caption says what the colours mean, and the only meaningful distinction (continuing states vs terminal states) is already carried by position and by the dashed vs solid loop line.
acceptance_test: Either add a one-line legend stating the colour semantics, or reduce the palette to two fills (continuing states vs terminal states) so that colour carries the one distinction the reader needs. Confirm the two classes remain distinguishable in grayscale.

issue: Caption states 'each depicted path a counterfactual completion', but one depicted terminal path is the limit-hit path ending in the 'Stopped' state (a non-completion / aborted request). 'Completion' is therefore inaccurate for that path; only the 'resolved' path is a true completion.
evidence: Caption: '...each depicted path a counterfactual completion, status [ILLUSTRATIVE].' Figure shows two terminal states: 'Final answer (emit, done)' and 'Stopped (limit, terminal)'.
acceptance_test: Reword the caption so the term covers both terminal outcomes (e.g., 'each depicted path a counterfactual trace/outcome'), or scope 'completion' explicitly to the resolved path only. A reader must not infer the Stopped path is a successful completion.

issue: The figure note claims 'tokens per submitted request grow ~2.5x under no prefix reuse', but the plotted retained-context bars grow from 9,500 to 12,960 tokens (1.36x), and the caption reports 24.9→34.0 GB (1.36x). If the 2.5x refers to cumulative processed/billed tokens in the 100-request ledger, the note does not show that calculation and the figure does not visualize it.
evidence: Note: 'tokens per submitted request grow ~2.5x under no prefix reuse (100-request ledger, Table 19-1)'. Panel (a) bars: 9,500 at turn 0, 12,960 at turn 4. Caption: 'from 24.9 GB single-shot to 34.0 GB at four turns'.
acceptance_test: Either change the note to 'retained context grows ~1.36x; cumulative processed tokens ~Xx' with the ledger calculation, or move the 2.5x claim to Table 19-1 and label the quantity explicitly.

figure: FIGURE 19.2 (Token growth vs resulting KV growth across agent turns)
issue: The two explanatory lines placed beneath the x-axes are set on colliding baselines and are also crowded against the panel-(b) tick labels, so the block reads as a single garbled smear rather than two sentences.
evidence: Rendered page shows the line 'counterfactual completion after four agent turns' and the line 'one final 300-token answer — not successive states of one live agent.' superimposed/overlapping in the band immediately below the '(single-shot) 0 1 2 3 4' tick labels of panel (b); the legend row ('initial context (L0) | retrieved (S=800) | generated (Y=65) | output (O=300)') is then stacked directly beneath the same crowded band.
acceptance_test: Re-render the page at 300 dpi and confirm (a) the two note lines are on distinct baselines with >= 2 pt leading and no glyph collision, (b) >= 4 pt clearance between the note block and the panel-(b) tick labels, and (c) >= 4 pt clearance between the note block and the legend row. If the two notes are intended as one sentence, merge them into a single line and re-flow.

issue: The combined legend is placed below a dense explanatory note rather than directly under the panels, forcing the reader to scan past a paragraph to decode the bars. The note sits between the x-axis labels and the legend.
evidence: Legend row appears below the note 'counterfactual: each column...'; the note is between the x-axis labels and the legend.
acceptance_test: Move the legend directly under the panels, above the note, or integrate the legend into the panel captions.

issue: The red annotation 'generated Y=65 turn' has no leader line, sits on top of the bar tops, and points at a component that is sub-pixel at this scale; it is also coloured red while the 'generated' segment it names is green.
evidence: In panel (a) the 'generated / Y=65 turn' text is drawn inside the plot area at roughly y = 12,000–13,000 tokens, overlapping the upper region of the turn-1/turn-2 bars. The 'generated (Y=65)' legend entry is green, yet the annotation is red (the colour of the 'output (O=300)' entry). At the plotted scale 65 tokens is 65/14000 of the axis, i.e. well under one pixel of bar height, so the reader cannot locate the segment the annotation names.
acceptance_test: Either (a) add a leader line from the annotation to the green segment of the turn-1 bar and re-colour the annotation to match the segment it names, or (b) delete the in-plot annotation and rely on the legend, adding a callout that states the generated share is not resolvable at this scale. Verify no glyph overlaps a bar edge at 300 dpi.

issue: The x-axis carries six tick labels ('(single-shot) 0 1 2 3 4') against five drawn bars, so the reader cannot determine which bar is the single-shot case and which is turn 0.
evidence: Panel (b) shows five red bars with five value labels (24.9, 27.2, 29.4, 31.7, 34.0) but the axis below is labelled '(single-shot) 0 1 2 3 4'. The caption says 'from 24.9 GB single-shot to 34.0 GB at four turns', which implies six distinct states (single-shot plus turns 0–4), while only five bars are drawn. Turn 0 and single-shot are numerically identical (9,200 + 300 = 9,500 tokens), so the ambiguity is benign arithmetically but not visually.
acceptance_test: Relabel the axis so the first bar reads 'single-shot' and the remaining four read 'turns 1–4' (or draw six bars and label them 'single-shot, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4'), and confirm the caption's 'from 24.9 GB single-shot to 34.0 GB at four turns' maps one-to-one onto the drawn bars.

issue: The per-bar value labels (24.9, 27.2, 29.4, 31.7, 34.0) are rotated 90 degrees, which is unnecessary for five short numbers and materially slows reading.
evidence: All five red value labels in panel (b) are set vertically above their bars; the same figure's panel (a) uses horizontal text throughout, so the two panels are typographically inconsistent.
acceptance_test: Set all five value labels horizontally above their bars, centred, with >= 2 pt clearance from the bar top and from the panel title; confirm the labels remain legible in grayscale (red on white is fine; verify the value is not lost against the bar's dot hatch).

issue: The four-entry legend is set as a single wide row that spans both panels and is squeezed into the same vertical band as the colliding note text, with no visual separation from the plot.
evidence: Legend row reads 'initial context (L0) | retrieved (S=800) | generated (Y=65) | output (O=300)' and sits directly beneath the overlapping note lines, with the swatches and labels rendered at the smallest type in the figure.
acceptance_test: Move the legend into a dedicated band with >= 6 pt clearance above and below, or split it into two rows centred under panel (a); confirm the legend type is >= 8 pt in the print proof and that the hatch patterns remain distinguishable in grayscale.
